text:
maya: Kicking off magnet-v1 embed bring-up. 5-fold holdout + short/query subset. Float32 baseline vs int8 & int6 quant. Sharing quick smoke numbers so we can decide next steps.

eval-bot: run 2026-03-22T15:12Z | id=run_8943 | model=magnet-v1 
configs: folds=5, k=[1,5,10], dataset=webqa-100k, short_queries=subset-3k

eval-bot: summary (macro avg over folds)
- float32: recall@1=0.882, recall@5=0.953, recall@10=0.969, mean_cos=0.412, nmi=0.61, silhouette=0.21
- int8 (symmetric): recall@1=0.872 (-1.0pt), recall@5=0.948 (-0.5pt), recall@10=0.965 (-0.4pt), mean_cos=0.407, nmi=0.60, silhouette=0.20
- int6 (quant-aware): recall@1=0.865 (-1.7pt), recall@5=0.944 (-0.9pt), recall@10=0.961 (-0.8pt), mean_cos=0.403, nmi=0.59, silhouette=0.19

maya: thanks. int8 loss looks small for overall recall but curious about short_queries slice.

eval-bot: short_queries subset (3k)
- float32: r@1=0.810, r@5=0.905
- int8: r@1=0.785 (-2.5pt), r@5=0.892 (-1.3pt)
- int6: r@1=0.768 (-4.2pt), r@5=0.880 (-2.5pt)

jonathan: ugh, larger drop on short queries. could be whitening/length normalization sensitivity. Did you run with per-sample norm?

maya: ran with L2 normalization on outputs. embedding pipeline: mean-center -> l2norm.

priya: can you dump UMAP plots for float32 vs int8? curious if cluster tightness changes for short queries.

maya: attaching quick visual (pasted inline). Observations: int8 clusters more diffuse for short query cohort, centroid shifts ~0.03 mean_cos.

sam: what's index config? PQ or raw HNSW? PQ can amplify small embedding shifts.

maya: FAISS HNSW with IVF-PQ on production-like index (PQ bytes=16). We also ran raw L2 brute for the bench to isolate embedding quality. The reported numbers above are brute-force.

leila: ok so quant introduces representational noise that hurts short queries more. Options:
- retune quant scale per-layer (symmetric->asymmetric?)
- per-channel quantization (we tried symmetric global)
- apply a small distillation pass to recalibrate final layer

jonathan: also consider calibrating a small offset correction on embeddings (whitening recalibration) before index-ing; cheap and sometimes recovers recall.

maya: action list:
1) run int8 per-channel quant (run id run_8944)
2) produce UMAP + centroid drift table for each fold
3) try whitening recalibration (PCA mean adjust) before L2 norm
4) check PQ sensitivity by running with PQ=8/16 bytes (brute vs pq)

priya: pls add short-query A/B eval (live sim) for top-100 queries from customer set. if int8 still down, we should hold off canary.

eval-bot: queued run_8944 (per-channel int8) started 2026-03-22T15:45Z

maya: quick note, bench command used:
```bash
python -m bench.embeddings --model magnet-v1 --dataset webqa-100k \\
  --folds 5 --k 1,5,10 --quant symmetric_int8 --index brute
```

sam: thanks. if per-channel fixes recall but costs >1.5x encode time, call out perf tradeoffs.

maya: will report latency/cpu/gpu encoding costs too.

jonathan: ping me when run_8944 finishes. if we can get <=0.7pt drop overall and <1.5pt on short queries I'm fine with a small canary.

leila: I'll draft canary config: 5% traffic, fallback to float32 variant on recall miss threshold.

maya: thanks — will update with run_8944 results and UMAPs.

eval-bot: run_8944 finished 2026-03-22T16:12Z | per-channel int8 summary:
- recall@1=0.879 (-0.3pt vs float32)
- short_queries r@1=0.803 (-0.7pt)
- mean_cos=0.410
- encoding throughput delta: +6% CPU cycles (quant overhead)

maya: nice, per-channel helps a lot. scheduling PQ-sensitivity jobs now.

priya: great. if PQ amplifies drift we'll need whitening before PQ.

sam: also add a tiny eval on multilingual subset (just in case).

maya: noted. will attach final ticket with plots + recommended canary config later today.

jonathan: thumbs up. :thumbsup:

leila: assigning follow-ups: maya -> run artifacts + ticket, priya -> short-query live list, sam -> perf tradeoff note.

maya: done, ticket RED-2219 created with artifacts link: https://redwood/issue/RED-2219

jonathan: thanks everyone.
